text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, said it expected citizens could start buying shares from the NPF portfolio for their privatisation bonds as of November 15.
- The Slovak subsidiary of Germany's Siemens has won a tender for a 20-year contract for modernisation and maintanence of the public lighting system in the capital Bratislava.
- Slovak tyre producer Matador Puchov will supply Czech car maker Skoda with tyres for its new Octavia model.
SME - Stefan Gavornik, chairman of the NPF, said he was considering resigning.
- The official Council for Slovak Television said it would propose the dismissal of STV director Jozaef Darmo at the next session of the parliament.
- The independent trade union of physicians LOZ said it would consider starting a protest strike in January next year if negotiations with employers fail to bring reults, mainly a salary increase.

- Slovakia's largest saving bank, Slovenska Sporitelna a.s., will provide 500 million crowns for the town Banska Bystrica in the form of municipal bonds and loans. The first tranche of the funds will be drawn through an issue of municipal bonds worth 250 million crowns.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Tax and customs duty evasion totalled 27.1 billion crowns in the first six months of this year, some 2.5 billion crowns more than in the same period last year.

- State budget revenues from taxes and custom duties totalled 67.6 billion crowns as of June 30, some 1.6 billion more than in the first haf 1995, representing about 46.6 percent of the planned sum for the full year.

- An extraordinary shareholders meeting of SEZ a.s. Dolny Kubin, an engineering firm producing equipment for the energy sector, approved an increase of the company's basic capital by some 10 percent, from the current 160 million crowns. The increase will be carried out through an issue of employee shares.
- Slovakia's annual consumption of natural gas as a primary energy source is expected to increase to 10 billion cubic metres in the year 2010, from the current 6.6 billion cubic metres.
